curatedRecords.title: Technical Artist Bootcamp: User Experience Design Applied to Technical Art
curatedRecords.use: The closest topic match: UX applied to tools made by a technical-art team. Use to motivate considering artists throughout development.
curatedRecords.status: Official indexed session description verified; tagged free content. Direct page retrieval failed on retry; full video not watched.

curatedRecords.title: The System of Tools: Reducing Frustration in a Daily Workflow
curatedRecords.use: Use the workflow-system framing for Maya → export → Unreal → verify. Friction can accumulate between tools as well as inside a panel.
curatedRecords.status: Official session description read; free-content listing. Full video not watched; no clip timestamps verified.

curatedRecords.title: Technical Artist Bootcamp: Production Values: Improving Quality, Longevity and Scalability
curatedRecords.use: PDF pages 32–35 discuss familiar interface conventions, hierarchy, grouping, defaults, and tool flow. A concrete LOD Tools example supports professional relevance.
curatedRecords.status: Free PDF text and speaker notes inspected; screenshot assets not extracted. Industry guidance, not a controlled study. Avoid turning fewer clicks into a universal goal.

curatedRecords.title: The User Experience of Game Development Tools
curatedRecords.use: Foundational game-tool UX preparation. Use as a broader resource after the directly applicable TA sessions.
curatedRecords.status: Free presentation surfaced by search; session synopsis reviewed, deck not read in full.

curatedRecords.title: Mapping User Stories in Agile
curatedRecords.use: Use a short artist journey to connect individual tasks to the overall workflow. A story map is larger than one role–goal–benefit sentence.
curatedRecords.status: Free article read. Teach only the small task-framing portion here; no Agile process prerequisite.

curatedRecords.title: Accounting for UX Work with User Stories in Agile Projects
curatedRecords.use: Useful instructor background for attaching usability criteria to a story.
curatedRecords.status: Free article reviewed through search extract. Do not turn this into sprint-management instruction.

curatedRecords.title: Paper Prototyping: Getting User Data Before You Code
curatedRecords.use: Test a sketched interface before implementation. Let the participant indicate actions and have a facilitator supply the next paper state.
curatedRecords.status: Free article read. Paper can reveal interpretation and flow issues; it cannot establish Unreal correctness or runtime performance.

curatedRecords.title: Usability Testing 101
curatedRecords.use: Use a realistic goal, observe the attempt, and record assistance. Distinguish what people do from their opinions about the design.
curatedRecords.status: Free article read. Student peer reviews are formative evidence, not representative validation of a professional tool.

curatedRecords.title: Parallel & Iterative Design
curatedRecords.use: Useful diagrams distinguish exploring alternatives from refining successive versions.
curatedRecords.status: Free article reviewed. Do not project its historical improvement percentages onto this class or Unreal tools.

curatedRecords.title: Mental Models
curatedRecords.use: People predict behavior using what they believe about a system. Ask what an artist expects before revealing the result.
curatedRecords.status: Free article read; professional synthesis, not an Unreal experiment.

curatedRecords.title: Memory Recognition and Recall in User Interfaces
curatedRecords.use: Visible options, paths, and examples can reduce the need to remember syntax or hidden state.
curatedRecords.status: Free guidance reviewed. Recognition does not imply showing every advanced setting simultaneously.

curatedRecords.title: Parallel Prototyping Leads to Better Design Results, More Divergence, and Increased Self-Efficacy
curatedRecords.use: A study of 33 participants designing web advertisements compared parallel and serial prototyping with equal time and feedback. The parallel condition performed better on the reported design outcomes. Teaching inference: compare a few layout alternatives before polishing one.
curatedRecords.status: Free author manuscript; methods, results, and discussion inspected. Participants were not professional designers; task was ad design, not editor-tool usability. No numerical gain transferred to Unreal.

curatedRecords.title: Beyond the five-user assumption: Benefits of increased sample sizes in usability testing
curatedRecords.use: The published abstract reports substantial variation in problems found by five-person samples drawn from 60 users. Small tests can help without guaranteeing that all important problems have been found.
curatedRecords.status: Free abstract only; full publisher article paywalled. Not required reading or a free full-paper recommendation.

curatedRecords.title: Principles of great design
curatedRecords.use: Useful chapters: agency 1:52, familiarity 6:04, simplicity 11:13. Transfer control, familiar behavior, and clear hierarchy to artist tools.
curatedRecords.status: Official transcript and chapter list read; video not watched end to end. These are design recommendations, not experimental proof.

curatedRecords.title: Essential Design Principles
curatedRecords.use: Mental-model explanation around 29:36–32:00. Use expectations to discuss why a familiar-looking control can still surprise a user.
curatedRecords.status: Official transcript excerpt verified; useful targeted segment, not a recommendation to watch the whole talk first.

curatedRecords.title: Feedback · Human Interface Guidelines
curatedRecords.use: Match interruption to consequence: routine status can stay near the work; significant, actionable risks can warrant interruption.
curatedRecords.status: Free guidance read. Adapt the principle to Unreal conventions; do not imitate Apple styling or assume all confirmations are helpful.

curatedRecords.title: Create and manage prototype flows
curatedRecords.use: Connected frames let an instructor demonstrate a starting state, action, and result. The documented flow feature is available on all plans and requires edit access.
curatedRecords.status: Official help read. A Figma file/account may be needed to author; no student account or installation required for this lesson.
